claims.text: Exactly what :func:`convene` would do, WITHOUT calling anything.
claims.why: The chunk shows dry_run_plan's own logic but not convene's full implementation; the claim about equality with convene cannot be fully verified here.

claims.text: No adapter method that could reach a vendor is touched: only the identity properties (actor, independence class, lane), which are pure.
claims.why: Within this chunk, dry_run_plan only accesses actor, independence_class, lane, vendor, model, endpoint; no method calls that could reach vendors.

claims.text: True only for a loopback HTTP endpoint. ``localhost``-ish and nothing else.
claims.why: The function checks the host against _LOCAL_HOSTS (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) after extracting from URL; matches the claim.

claims.text: "Local" was a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set; here it is a property of the RESOLVED host, checked, not asserted.
claims.why: The claim about an environment variable is not verifiable from this chunk; the function does check the resolved host, but the historical context is uncheckable.

claims.text: Lanes come from the council profiles, NOT from a default argument here: ``codex`` and ``agy`` are ``untrusted`` (allow-list tier ON) unless the operator opts in per council.
claims.why: The function constructs adapters with common args; lane is not set here except for OllamaAdapter where it is explicitly passed. The claim about 'council profiles' and default behavior of codex/agy is not directly visible in this chunk; the adapters' defaults are not shown.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY and ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is neither read for routing nor written -- normalising a remote Ollama into this process would retroactively falsify ``offload.py``'s ``lane="trusted"`` justification from a code path nobody edited.
claims.why: The function uses ollama_host or DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST; it does not read OLLAMA_HOST here, but the claim about offload.py's justification is external to this chunk.

claims.text: A seat that can reach a real vendor was offered without ``live=True``.
claims.why: The class is defined as a RuntimeError subclass, and its name and docstring match the intent; no code contradicts it.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a ``ValueError``: every other refusal in :func:`convene` is a malformed-roster complaint, and "you were about to spend money" must be catchable on its own.
claims.why: The class is a RuntimeError, not ValueError, but the claim about other refusals in convene being ValueError is not fully verifiable in this chunk; though convene raises ValueError for empty participants and duplicates, the full set of refusals is not shown.

claims.text: Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor.  FAIL-CLOSED.
claims.why: The function iterates participants and counts a seat as live unless one of the listed conditions holds; the logic is fail-closed (assumes live unless proven otherwise).

claims.text: The question is not "is this class from :mod:`vendors`" -- it is "if ``ask()`` runs, does SHIPPED transport code execute".
claims.why: The function checks _dispatch module and _runner/_chat hooks; it does not directly check ask() execution, but the logic is consistent with the claim; however, the claim about ask() is not directly testable here.

claims.text: A seat is therefore counted as LIVE unless one of these is demonstrably true: * it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all (the base ``CouncilAdapter._dispatch`` raises ``NotImplementedError``, so a class defined elsewhere is the caller's own code and the caller owns it); * its ``_dispatch`` -- the transport seam -- is defined OUTSIDE :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors`, i.e. the test/host replaced it; * its ``runner`` / ``chat`` hook is not one of :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS`, i.e. a substitute was injected at construction.
claims.why: The function implements exactly these conditions: checks if adapter is instance of shipped_classes, checks _dispatch.__module__, and checks _runner/_chat against _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS.

claims.text: Everything else -- including an adapter shape this function has never seen -- is assumed able to spend money.
claims.why: If none of the three conditions are met, the seat is added to live list; the logic defaults to live.

claims.text: If :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: The code checks `if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS:` before checking hooks; if empty, it skips the hook check, thus not marking as substituted, which means the seat remains live (fail-closed).

claims.text: ``trusted_vendors`` is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only.
claims.why: The code uses trusted_vendors to set adapter.lane='trusted' for matching vendors; it is per-council and explicit.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False.  Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_seats`) raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: The code checks `if not live:` and calls live_egress_seats, raising LiveCouncilRefused if seats exist; this happens before council_id, store, and roster chaining.

claims.text: Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The function only raises if live_egress_seats returns non-empty; offline adapters would be filtered out, but the claim about the replay harness is external.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach `sorted()` empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: The code does `participants = tuple(participants)` before any iteration, converting to tuple to avoid iterator draining.

claims.text: FIRST, above every other check: a refusal that happened after the roster was chained would leave an open council on disk that nobody closed, and a refusal that happened after dispatch would not be one.
claims.why: The live gate is placed immediately after the empty-participant check and before other checks like duplicate identities, matching the comment.

observations.what: The live gate in convene is placed before duplicate identity checks, which may allow a spend refusal to occur before roster validation, but that is consistent with the docstring's priority.
default_participants uses `ollama_host or DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST`; if ollama_host is an empty string, it falls back to default, which may be unexpected but not incorrect.

The `_is_local_http` function uses regex `^https?://([^/:]+)` which captures the host but does not handle IPv6 addresses in brackets; however, _LOCAL_HOSTS includes '::1' which would not match because the regex would capture '[::1]'? Actually the regex captures up to ':' or '/', so '[::1]' would be captured as '[::1]' which is not in _LOCAL_HOSTS, so 'http://[::1]:8000' would not be considered local despite '::1' being in the set.

In live_egress_seats, the check `getattr(dispatch, "__module__", "") != _vendors.__name__` relies on _vendors being imported; if _vendors is None or lacks __name__, this could raise AttributeError, but the code assumes it is a module.
The `convene` function sets `adapter.lane = "trusted"` for trusted vendors, mutating the adapter objects passed in, which may have side effects outside the council run.

risks: _is_local_http | medium | IPv6 loopback addresses in brackets are not recognized as local, causing a remote-seeming classification for local IPv6 endpoints | Test with 'http://[::1]:8000' to see if it returns False
